jobs.title: Government Affairs Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
SentiLink helps institutions and protects customers by accurately resolving identities and flagging fraud risk. Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.


Role:

SentiLink is expanding its government affairs work in Washington, DC and in a growing number of states, and we’re looking for a sharp, policy-savvy Government Affairs Manager to lead advocacy strategy with Congress, federal regulators, and industry coalitions, and to direct SentiLink’s full bench of state and federal lobbyists. In addition to advancing federal policy initiatives and direct lobbying, you’ll work closely with Public Sector sales, marketing/comms, and executive leadership to help shape the policy environment that supports SentiLink’s mission.

This role gives you real ownership: you’ll set the strategy and cadence for every contracted lobbyist we work with, in Washington and in the states, so our advocacy stays sharp and our team is better enabled and more effective when they walk into the room with the right people.

This role reports to the Head of Public Policy & External Affairs, and inherits a function with clear priorities and foundation already in place, with the expectation that you’ll expand it. It will require frequent in-person engagement with stakeholders across the DC area, including Capitol Hill (House and Senate, Republicans and Democrats), federal agencies, and industry events.

This role requires you to be based out of Washington, DC.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead day-to-day federal advocacy, building and maintaining relationships across Congressional offices in both parties and chambers, with particular depth on Financial Services/Banking, Ways and Means/Finance, and Appropriations committee staff.

  • Direct SentiLink’s bench of contracted federal and state lobbyists and consultants, setting priorities and a regular cadence of engagement, and translating their work into the budget-cycle and procurement insight our Public Sector sellers need to close.

  • Serve as a trusted resource on policy issues affecting identity verification, fraud prevention, and financial services, in direct support of Public Sector sales cycles (RFP language, identity standards, procurement timing).

  • Lead engagement with trade associations and coalitions (RDA, ETA, CBA, ABA, and similar), managing SentiLink’s participation and extracting more value from existing memberships.

  • Build a state-level ability to monitor and report on state legislative and regulatory developments on issues related to data brokers, privacy and identity.

  • Prepare briefing materials and talking points for internal and external stakeholders, and represent SentiLink in meetings, hearings, roundtables, and industry events.

Requirements:

  • 4+ years of experience in public policy, government relations, or legislative affairs, ideally with a combination of time on Capitol Hill, at a trade association, or a regulated fintech/financial services environment.

  • Working knowledge of federal legislative and regulatory processes, especially related to financial services or identity, and the ability to pick up state-level processes quickly.

  • Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills with bipartisan credibility. You've built (or are excited to build) working relationships across the aisle, House and Senate, not just within one party's orbit.

  • Excellent writing and public speaking ability: comfortable drafting comment letters, testimony, and briefing memos, and representing SentiLink on a conference panel or in a room of policymakers with equal confidence.

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with data.

  • A proactive, self-starting mindset and the ability to thrive in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment.

  • Genuine interest in going deep on fraud, identity, privacy and data policy. This is not a generalist policy seat; you'll be expected to develop real subject-matter depth quickly.


Bonus Points:

  • Familiarity with state legislative tracking tools.

  • Exposure to public sector sales cycles or government procurement.

  • Background in identity verification, fraud prevention, or tech policy.


Compensation:

150,000 - 190,000 year + equity + benefits

Perks:

  • Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

Corporate Values:

  • Follow Through

  • Deep Understanding

  • Whatever It Takes

  • Do Something Smart

As a Senior Data Scientist at SentiLink, you will build our core products: models that identify fraudsters and also advance our growing suite of products in financial risk. As an experienced researcher you will be relied upon to be technically capable and the definitive owner of your respective domain. You will often work on projects with high visibility and impact that require deep domain understanding, critical thinking and strong technical abilities. You will work with teams across the company to research new types of fraud, develop new products, and provide analysis to drive sales and marketing. This is a full-stack data science role, involving model development, analysis, and writing production code. You should be interested in having end-to-end ownership and a fast-moving environment where deep domain understanding drives development and unusual insights drive our competitive advantage rather than optimization of new machine learning methodologies.

We have open roles on multiple teams including:

  • Emerging Products - focuses on 0-to-1 development of new offerings brought to market

  • Application Fraud - analyzes the foundational elements of consumer financial applications to detect all forms of fraud

  • Identity - resolves identities across massive, often conflicting data sources (both digital and physical) and generates risk models from limited information

Technologies: Python 3, PostgreSQL, and AWS infrastructure (EC2, S3, RDS, Redshift, etc.)

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain SentiLink’s fraud detection models through the full model development lifespan: from data acquisition decisions through featurization, focusing labeling resources, model training, experimentation, productionalization, and monitoring.

  • Build foundational modeling to drive SentiLink’s expanding suite of Fraud and Financial Risk products.

  • Research new types of fraud and develop new SentiLink products around identity verification.

  • Achieve success by researching / developing through iteration, integration of new data sources and inventive feature engineering.

  • Write production-ready code that can be relied on for real-time decision making by our partners.

  • Design, perform, and present analyses that will inform data acquisition, product development, risk operations priorities, marketing, and sales efforts.

  • Work with engineering, risk operations, and data acquisitions to access necessary data, maintain data quality, and support data access

Requirements:

  • 4+ years relevant work experience & relevant PhD or 6+ years & relevant Masters

  • Proven track record of solving complex / high profile business problems with DS / ML solutions

  • Experience in communicating outcomes / progress to senior management / stakeholders

  • Very strong in “end to end” DS development: Planning, fleshing out success criteria / metrics, getting buy-in, developing the solution, delivering the solution (prod / deck / strategy doc / etc)

  • Strong practical ML / Stats knowledge, i.e. can easily employ the suite of standard ML / stats tools to quickly scope out solutions, and double down where needed. Experience with SOTA ML solutions is a plus

  • Interest in developing deep domain expertise for product-focused work: a background in fraud is not required, but willingness to learn is

  • Experience writing production code and tests

  • Detail oriented and thoughtful - someone we can rely on to make business-changing decisions

  • Bonus for familiarity with: identity solutions, fintech, or adjacent industries

  • Experience working at a startup strongly preferred

  • Thrive in a fast paced environment characterized by the need to solve extremely varied, high impact, open ended problems.

  • Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States and must live in the United States

  • $200,000/year - $240,000/year + equity + benefits

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Home office stipend, and more!

  • Experience working with airlines, hotels, online travel agencies, travel marketplaces, hospitality companies, ticketing platforms, venues, or entertainment businesses preferred

  • Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and highly driven in fast-paced startup environments

  • Excellent communication, relationship-building, and strategic selling skills

  • Established network within travel, hospitality, entertainment, fraud, identity, security, payments, operations, or digital teams is a plus

  • Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States and must live in the United States

$275,000-$350,000/year OTE + equity + benefits

Perks:

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

  • Conduct hands-on penetration testing and vulnerability research against SentiLink's infrastructure and applications

  • Partner with engineering teams to remediate findings and embed security into the development process without slowing them down

  • Participate in the security on-call rotation, including incident response and regular response testing

  • Contribute to threat modeling and security design reviews for new systems, with a focus on cloud integrations and identity flows

  • Stay current on offensive security techniques, AI-assisted security tooling, and emerging attack patterns relevant to fintech and identity verification

Requirements:

  • 8+ years of experience in security engineering, software engineering with a security focus, or closely related roles

  • Proficient in at least one systems language (Go, Rust, C++) and at least one higher-level language (Python, TypeScript)

  • Proven ability to design and ship production software end-to-end

  • Deep AWS infrastructure expertise, including IAM, EKS, RDS, networking, and managed services

  • Proficiency with using an AI tool such as Claude Code, ChatGPT/Codex, Cursor or another similar tool

  • Demonstrated ability to identify security misconfigurations and vulnerabilities across cloud architectures, application code, and the integrations between them

  • Experience conducting or building tooling for penetration testing, vulnerability assessment, or red team activities

  • Track record of building security automation and tooling from scratch

  • Comfortable operating independently on ambiguous problems without heavy process or oversight

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to partner with engineers who are not security specialists

Nice to have:

  • Experience building or deploying LLM-based agents or AI-assisted security tooling

  • Prior experience at a security product company (Wiz, Snyk, Datadog, etc.) or other security-forward engineering org

  • Prior fintech, identity, or fraud detection experience

  • Industry certifications (OSCP, OSCE, GPEN, GXPN)

  • Experience with detection engineering or SIEM platforms

  • Published security research, CVEs, or open source security tooling contributions

  • Experience supporting compliance frameworks (FedRAMP, SOC 2, PCI DSS) without it being their primary focus

$220k-300k/year + equity + benefits

Perks:

  • Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

Role:

SentiLink builds the fraud detection and identity verification models much of the US financial system runs on. Each one has to pass review by our customers' model risk teams, regulators, and auditors without slowing how fast we ship. You'll own that domain end to end.

You'll lead a team of 3+ data scientists. You won't build our fraud products; your team measures, stress-tests, explains, and monitors them. It's a management role that stays hands-on: you'll review code, challenge methodology, and step in where needed.

The role includes real modeling work: assurance models that audit our production models, find gaps in how our products behave, and produce unbiased evaluation metrics.

We use AI in model risk today, but mostly in one-off projects. You'll make it a first-tier tool that scales what the team can do, putting you at the cutting edge of AI in model risk and governance.

You'll also work directly with model risk teams at some of the biggest banks and financial institutions in the space. Governance gates how fast they adopt our products, so this role is a direct lever on growth.

This is a remote, US-based role.

Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, AWS (S3, Redshift, SageMaker), pandas, scikit-learn, XGBoost, MLflow, and modern LLM tooling.

What You'll Do:

  • Manage a team of 3+ data scientists and set how they work.

  • Own strategy and execution for model risk: roadmap, priorities, and what we automate or standardize.

  • Own the technical core: performance and drift monitoring, validation, calibration and stability testing, fair lending and bias assessments, model inventory, and change management.

  • Build assurance models that audit production models, surface product gaps, and produce unbiased evaluation metrics.

  • Move AI from one-off projects to a first-tier tool across the team's work.

  • Act as an independent technical counterpart to Applied ML: review methodology and translate model changes into risk impact.

  • Produce validation reports and documentation for leadership, customers, auditors, and regulators, and track findings to remediation.

  • Work with partner model risk teams at major banks and FIs, alongside Partner Success.

This is a high-leverage role. Governance gates how quickly our customers can adopt what we build, which makes it a direct lever on the company's growth, with substantial room for the right person to define it and grow with it.

What We're Looking For:

  • 6+ years applying statistics, ML, or quantitative analytics in industry, including 3+ years managing DS, analytics, or quant risk teams.

  • Background in at least one of: model or portfolio risk analytics; modeling in a supporting or consulting role, internal or external; large-scale analytics, reporting, or BI.

  • Degree in Statistics, Math, CS, Economics, Physics, or another quantitative field.

  • Strong hands-on Python, including building recurring pipelines, monitoring, or reporting. Working knowledge of Git and SQL.

  • Experience with cloud data and compute: object storage like S3 and remote compute like SageMaker or Databricks. AWS preferred.

  • Able to read a model and interrogate its methodology: performance evaluation, calibration, drift, backtesting, and fairness.

  • Track record of measurable business impact, end to end.

  • Proficient with AI tools in daily work: effective prompting, building and using agent skills, and AI-assisted coding and analysis.

  • Sound judgment with sensitive data, and clear communication with technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Math, Statistics, CS, Engineering, Economics, or related STEM)

  • Must be legally authorized to work in and reside in the US

Nice to haves:

  • Familiarity with SR 11-7, SR 26-2, OCC guidance, or fair lending.

  • Experience working with model risk teams at banks or fintechs, auditors, or regulators.

  • Fraud, identity, credit, or financial risk model experience.

  • Experience building or scaling a validation, governance, or analytics function.

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

Role:

We’re looking for a strong Senior Engineering Manager to lead a backend/platform-focused engineering team responsible for powering SentiLink’s core products.

This team owns the backend systems, external APIs, and services that power these experiences, as well as the technical foundation that ensures the product is scalable, reliable, and secure.

You will lead a small but growing team of engineers responsible for building API-driven systems, evolving our platform architecture, and enabling product teams to move quickly with confidence.

This role sits at the intersection of backend platform development, technical architecture, and people leadership. You’ll partner closely with product, data science, infrastructure, and front-end engineering teams to deliver high-quality systems in a fast-moving environment.

We are looking for a manager who is fundamentally a strong backend engineer and enjoys staying close to technical work, contributing to architecture, guiding design decisions, and unblocking complex systems challenges.

This is a remote, US-based position.

Technologies: React, Golang, Python, PostgreSQL (RDS), Docker, OpenSearch, AWS technologies (Lambda, Cognito and other standard services)

Responsibilities:

  • Lead and grow a team of 10 Senior & Staff backend/platform engineers building the systems that power Intercept and other critical applications

  • Drive execution across planning, prioritization, and delivery with a focus on reliability and scalability

  • Own the technical direction of backend services and APIs, ensuring systems are secure, performant, and maintainable

  • Partner with product and front-end teams to translate product requirements into robust backend architectures

  • Collaborate with data science to productionize models and integrate decisioning systems into APIs and workflows

  • Work closely with infrastructure to improve system reliability, observability, and developer experience

  • Contribute to architectural decisions and guide the long-term evolution of our platform

  • Maintain high standards for code quality, testing, and operational excellence

  • Support incident response and ensure systems meet SLA expectations

  • Hire, mentor, and develop engineers while maintaining a high hiring bar

  • Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement

  • Contribute to code and technical problem-solving as needed

Requirements:

  • 3-7 years of engineering management experience leading backend or platform teams

  • Strong background as a senior or staff-level backend engineer

  • Deep experience building API-driven systems using languages like Golang, Python, or similar

  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, scalability, and system design

  • Experience owning and evolving backend architecture in production environments

  • Track record of shipping complex, customer-facing or platform systems

  • Comfortable leading technical discussions and diving into implementation details

  • Experience working in fast-paced, startup or growth-stage environments

  • Experience building platforms that support product teams (internal APIs, shared services, developer tooling) preferred

  • Familiarity with data-intensive systems, search (OpenSearch), or risk/decisioning systems preferred

  • Experience in fintech or highly regulated environments preferred

Compensation:

$200,000/year - $260,000/year + equity + benefits

Perks:

  • Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

Corporate Values:

  • Follow Through

  • Deep Understanding

  • Whatever It Takes

  • Do Something Smart

Role:

As an Enterprise Account Executive, Utilities, you will lead SentiLink’s expansion across the retail energy ecosystem, including competitive energy suppliers, retail electricity providers (REPs), retail natural gas providers, community choice aggregators (CCAs), utility-adjacent service providers, energy marketplaces, and energy technology platforms. You’ll partner with organizations facing complex challenges in identity verification, fraud prevention, customer onboarding, account security, payment risk, and compliance across their customer acquisition and account management experiences.

Your energy industry expertise will extend well beyond traditional sales - we're looking to you to help define our retail energy go-to-market strategy, develop playbooks for the vertical, and identify new opportunities across the broader energy ecosystem.

This is a remote, US-based role.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop the retail energy vertical by identifying, prioritizing, and engaging retail electricity providers, retail natural gas providers, community choice aggregators, energy retailers, energy marketplaces, and energy technology platforms

  • Own the entire sales cycles from prospecting through close, including discovery, business case development, solution positioning, and commercial negotiations

  • Help define SentiLink’s retail energy go-to-market strategy, messaging, and use cases

  • Build trusted relationships with fraud, risk, customer operations, revenue protection, credit, compliance, customer experience, and digital transformation leaders

  • Navigate complex organizations and align stakeholders across operational, technical, and executive teams

  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Marketing, Partnerships, and Customer Success to drive successful customer outcomes

  • Stay current on evolving fraud trends, customer acquisition challenges, regulatory developments, and identity-related risks impacting energy providers

Requirements:

  • 5+ years of enterprise sales experience, preferably selling SaaS solutions into retail energy, utilities, fintech, telecommunications, or financial services organizations

  • Demonstrated success selling into complex enterprise environments using a multi-stakeholder sales motion

  • Experience working with retail energy providers, utilities, energy marketplaces, energy technology companies, or customer acquisition organizations preferred

  • Strong understanding of customer onboarding, identity verification, fraud prevention, account security, payment risk, revenue protection, credit risk, or compliance workflows preferred

  • Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and highly driven in fast-paced startup environments

  • Excellent communication, relationship-building, and strategic selling skills

  • Established network within retail energy, utilities, fraud, risk, customer operations, credit, compliance, or digital transformation teams is a plus

  • Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States and must live in the United States

Compensation:

  • $275,000/year - $350,000/year OTE + equity + benefits

Perks:

  • Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

Corporate Values:

  • Follow Through

  • Deep Understanding

  • Whatever It Takes

  • Do Something Smart

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

Role:

SentiLink is hiring a Head of Marketing (B2B) to build and lead a well-run, high-performing marketing organization that accelerates organizational momentum and drives revenue targets. You will set the strategy, put the right people in the right seats, and create the focus, cohesion, and accountability needed to turn marketing investment into meaningful pipeline and ARR.

Leadership is the most important part of this role. You will establish clear ownership, develop and empower a high-performing team, and create an operating rhythm that enables fast execution, learning, and iteration. This role reports to the Chief Revenue Officer.

This role is for a deeply experienced B2B software marketer who has built and scaled programs for technical products, sophisticated buyers, and complex enterprise sales cycles. You will partner closely with Sales, Product Marketing, Product, Data Science, Revenue Operations, and executive leadership to drive commercial outcomes. Knowledge of identity or fraud is a bonus.

This is a remote, US-based role, and we expect an accelerated interview and hiring process.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and lead a cohesive, high-performing marketing organization by assessing the team, putting the right people in the right seats, clarifying ownership, coaching talent, and creating accountability for outcomes.

  • Set the marketing strategy and operating rhythm, making clear decisions about priorities, team structure, and investment while creating a bias toward speed, learning, and iteration.

  • Own SentiLink’s B2B marketing strategy and execution, with accountability for meaningful qualified pipeline, conversion, revenue, and ARR growth. Define an efficient pipeline-generation philosophy; do not default to adding BDR headcount or optimizing for high-volume activity.

  • Develop and execute an integrated campaign calendar, prioritizing the campaigns and products with the greatest revenue potential. Run full-stack B2B campaigns and multi-touch nurture programs from audience strategy and content through distribution, sales coordination, measurement, and optimization.

  • Partner with Sales to create strategic account growth programs for large, complex enterprise organizations.

  • Own SentiLink’s brand and digital growth engine, including website strategy, conversion-focused content experiences, SEO, and AEO.

  • Build on SentiLink’s strength in events, webinars, executive programs, and field marketing while creating clear ownership, cohesive execution, and a direct connection to pipeline and revenue outcomes.

  • Build measurement and reporting around pipeline, conversion, revenue, and ARR. Partner with Product Marketing, Product, Data Science, Revenue Operations, and executive leadership to turn market insight into compelling campaigns and customer narratives.

Requirements:

  • 7+ years of B2B marketing experience, including significant experience in B2B SaaS, infrastructure software, cybersecurity, fintech, or another technical enterprise software business. Knowledge of identity or fraud is a bonus.

  • Demonstrated success leading and developing marketing teams, including hiring, team design, coaching, performance management, and building a cohesive organization with clear ownership.

  • An energizing, direct, accountable, and collaborative leadership style. You create clarity, address hard problems, move with urgency, and raise the level of the people around you.

  • A track record of building B2B pipeline programs that contributed to meaningful revenue and ARR, with the ability to explain the strategy, execution, tradeoffs, and outcomes in detail.

  • A strong point of view on efficient pipeline generation and the right mix of campaigns, content, channels, sales partnership, events, partnerships, and team capabilities.

  • Experience running integrated B2B campaigns and multi-touch nurture programs across multiple channels.

  • Experience marketing to sophisticated enterprise buying committees and building strategic account growth programs that reach the right stakeholders and create commercial movement.

  • Hands-on experience with website strategy, SEO, AEO, content, brand, and conversion optimization, plus strong commercial judgment in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

  • Experience partnering closely with enterprise Sales and executive stakeholders; experience with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, or similar platforms

  • Willingness to travel up to 25%

  • Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States and must live in the United States

Domain experience in fraud, identity, fintech, or financial services is not required. Experience marketing to financial institutions, fintechs, marketplaces, or other regulated industries is a plus.

Compensation:

$260,000-$275,000 base salary + bonus, equity, and benefits

Compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, qualifications, and level.

Perks:

  • Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

Corporate Values:

  • Follow Through

  • Deep Understanding

  • Whatever It Takes

  • Do Something Smart

SentiLink helps institutions and protects customers by accurately resolving identities and flagging fraud risk. Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.


Role:

SentiLink is building high-performing teams to tackle some of the most complex problems in identity, risk, and fraud, and we are looking for a Lead/Staff Technical Recruiter to play a critical role in that growth.

In this role, you will own full cycle recruiting for technical roles across Engineering and Data Science, while remaining flexible to support business and go-to-market hiring as company priorities evolve. You will also partner closely with leadership on complex and high-impact searches, including leadership roles.

This is a highly collaborative role for a recruiter who brings strong talent-market expertise, sound judgment, and a willingness to operate as a fungible recruiting partner across the organization. You will be a trusted advisor to hiring managers, help shape hiring strategy, and provide informal leadership and mentorship to other recruiters and recruiting partners.

This is a remote, U.S.-based position. Candidates based in Austin who are able to work regularly from one of our office locations are especially encouraged to apply.

Responsibilities:

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across technical, business, and GTM functions, from individual contributor through leadership level roles

  • Partner with hiring managers and senior leaders on role definition, leveling, talent-market strategy, candidate evaluation, and hiring decisions

  • Lead sourcing strategies and build high-quality pipelines for specialized and competitive talent markets

  • Manage complex and high-priority searches, proactively identifying risks and driving alignment across stakeholders

  • Use a data-driven approach to recruiting strategy, leveraging funnel metrics to prioritize work, improve conversion rates, and drive hiring outcomes

  • Deliver structured, consistent, and high-quality interview and candidate experiences

  • Maintain strong operational rigor across the ATS and recruiting workflows

  • Improve recruiting processes, tools, and practices to increase efficiency, consistency, and scale

  • Provide informal team leadership through mentorship, calibration, and knowledge sharing

  • Help embed thoughtful, AI-enabled practices across our recruiting infrastructure and team, using AI to improve sourcing, market research, workflow efficiency, candidate experience, and recruiting operations while maintaining sound judgment and confidentiality

 

Requirements:

  • 7+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including significant technical recruiting experience in a technology company or high-growth startup

  • Experience recruiting across Engineering, Data Science, and/or Product, as well as business or GTM functions

  • Demonstrated success recruiting both technical individual contributors and people leaders, including Manager- and Director-level candidates

  • Proven ability to influence hiring managers and senior leaders through market insight, sound judgment, and clear communication

  • Strong sourcing, pipeline development, candidate assessment, and closing skills

  • Data-driven approach to recruiting, including experience using funnel metrics to improve hiring outcomes

  • Demonstrated fluency with AI tools and workflows, with the judgment to identify practical use cases, evaluate outputs, and help drive responsible adoption across a recruiting team

  • Experience mentoring, coaching, or informally leading other recruiters or sourcers

  • Strong stakeholder management, prioritization, and operational discipline; experience with Ashby is preferred

  • Commitment to inclusive hiring practices, confidentiality, and values-aligned teams

  • Willingness to travel approximately six times per year for company meetups, off-sites, and relevant events

  • Must be authorized to work in the U.S. and reside within the country

  • Candidates based in Austin and willing to work regularly from the office are preferred

Compensation:

$160,000-$200,000/year + equity + benefits

Perks:

  • Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

Corporate Values:

  • Follow Through

  • Deep Understanding

  • Whatever It Takes

  • Do Something Smart

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. Role:

SentiLink is seeking an experienced fraud leader to serve as a trusted advisor to prospective customers, primarily large financial institutions and other financial-services organizations.

In this role, you will engage directly with fraud, risk, identity, and financial-crime executives to understand their challenges and help them determine how SentiLink’s products can be operationalized within their existing workflows. You will bring practical experience from the field to customer conversations, connecting fraud strategy, risk operations, technology, and business outcomes.

You will help prospects think through questions such as:

  • Where SentiLink’s products fit within their fraud and identity-risk processes

  • How to integrate our solutions into existing systems, teams, and decisioning workflows

  • How to design effective operating models, controls, and escalation paths

  • How to measure impact across fraud loss, customer experience, operational efficiency, and risk

This is a highly consultative, customer-facing role. Success will require the credibility to engage senior executives, the practical judgment to translate complex fraud challenges into actionable recommendations, and the ability to collaborate closely with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as a fraud subject-matter expert in conversations with prospective customers.

  • Build trusted relationships with fraud, risk, identity, payments, and financial-crime executives.

  • Lead discovery conversations to understand customers’ fraud strategies, workflows, pain points, and priorities.

  • Advise prospects on how to incorporate SentiLink’s products into their operational and technology environments.

  • Translate customer needs into clear recommendations for product configuration, workflow design, implementation, and change management.

  • Support sales engagements, executive briefings, workshops, demonstrations, and responses to complex customer questions.

  • Partner with Sales to develop compelling, credible, and outcome-oriented customer narratives.

  • Share customer insights with Product and Engineering to inform roadmap priorities and solution design.

  • Help establish best practices for fraud prevention, identity verification, risk management, and financial-crime operations.

  • Represent SentiLink at industry events, customer meetings, and other external forums.

  • Track emerging fraud patterns, attack techniques, regulatory developments, and industry practices.

 

Requirements:

  • 10+ years of experience in fraud, fraud risk, financial crime, identity, trust and safety, or a related field.

  • Significant experience in a senior fraud leadership or practitioner role within a bank, lender, payments company, fintech,, or other regulated financial-services organization.

  • Deep understanding of fraud operations, risk decisioning, identity, investigations, or financial-crime processes.

  • Experience designing, managing, or improving fraud workflows and operating models.

  • Demonstrated ability to build rapport and credibility quickly with senior executives.

  • Strong understanding of how fraud teams evaluate, implement, and operationalize technology solutions.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.

  • Ability to translate complex fraud and technical concepts for executive, operational, and technical audiences.

  • Strong commercial judgment and comfort operating in a consultative, customer-facing environment.

  • Ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.

  • High ownership, sound judgment, and a bias toward action.

  • Deep curiosity about evolving fraud tactics, identity risk, and the broader risk landscape.

 

Compensation:

$180,000–$250,000 base + equity + benefits

Actual compensation will depend on experience, level, and the scope of the role ultimately aligned during the hiring process.

 

Perks:

  • Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

Corporate Values:

  • Follow Through

  • Deep Understanding

  • Whatever It Takes

  • Do Something Smart

  • Collaborate with Data Science to make mobile device signals available for fraud detection models and support effective use of those signals.

  • Demonstrated ability to build technically complex mobile software with an emphasis on systems-level engineering rather than primarily user interface development.

  • Strong ability to independently explore and solve ambiguous technical problems with a high degree of ownership and autonomy.

  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, and interpersonal skills.

  • Deep understanding of device fingerprinting approaches and mechanisms preferred.

  • Experience partnering with data scientists to provide signals or capabilities used in machine learning models preferred.

We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

Role:

SentiLink's Information Security team is responsible for protecting our systems, data, and customers while enabling the business to operate securely and efficiently. We work closely with Engineering, IT, Legal, Product, and business teams to manage security risks, maintain regulatory compliance, and build effective security controls across the organization.

We're looking for a Director of Security & Risk to lead our security governance, compliance, assurance, and risk management programs. This is a leadership role with broad ownership across FedRAMP, SOC 2, PCI DSS, customer and partner security assessments, third-party risk, and security policy.

This is not a traditional GRC role. SentiLink operates a highly technical, AWS-based environment, and many of the risks and compliance requirements we manage require deep technical understanding. We're looking for someone who can independently evaluate technical risks, understand security architecture and proposed remediations, and work effectively with engineers, auditors, regulators, and business stakeholders.

You will lead and develop a team of security and compliance professionals, establish priorities, identify gaps in our existing programs, and develop a roadmap for improving our security posture. We expect you to bring the experience and judgment to identify problems and opportunities independently, rather than simply execute an existing plan.

You will report to SentiLink's security leader and work closely with Security Engineering, which remains a separate function responsible for technical security architecture and implementation.

Success in this role means building a proactive, effective, and scalable security program that goes beyond passing audits to meaningfully reducing organizational risk.

This is a remote, US-based position.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead and develop SentiLink's security governance, risk, and compliance organization. Manage and mentor security and compliance professionals, evaluate program effectiveness, identify gaps in expertise and capacity, and develop organizational and hiring plans as the company grows.

  • Own SentiLink's security compliance and audit programs, including FedRAMP, SOC 2, and PCI DSS. Lead external assessments, manage control effectiveness and evidence collection, oversee Vanta and compliance automation, and ensure the organization continuously meets its obligations rather than preparing only for periodic audits.

  • Drive the ongoing maturity of SentiLink's government security program. Oversee FedRAMP continuous monitoring, POA&M governance, change-management compliance, agency-specific requirements, and assessment readiness. Anticipate evolving requirements, including FedRAMP 20x, and develop plans to address them.

  • Establish and operate a rigorous security risk management program. Own the identification, assessment, documentation, escalation, and treatment of security risks, control deficiencies, and exceptions. Ensure material risks receive appropriate attention and that remediation is tracked through completion.

  • Lead SentiLink's third-party security risk management program. Establish and enforce risk-based vendor diligence requirements, improve assessment quality, manage ongoing vendor oversight, and ensure material security concerns are resolved or appropriately escalated before approval.

  • Own customer and partner security assurance. Lead complex security assessments and audits from financial institutions, government agencies, and other partners. Evaluate contractual security requirements in collaboration with Legal, coordinate technical responses, and ensure security representations are accurate, complete, and defensible.

  • Own security policy and control governance. Maintain security policies, standards, and control frameworks, ensuring requirements are appropriately mapped across regulatory obligations, reflected in actual operations, and periodically evaluated for effectiveness.

  • Continuously improve the effectiveness and scalability of security programs. Develop clear accountability, measurable outcomes, repeatable processes, and automation. Proactively identify emerging risks and requirements, communicate recommendations to leadership, and drive improvements across organizational boundaries.

Requirements:

  • 10+ years of experience in information security, including significant experience leading security governance, compliance, assurance, or risk management programs.

  • Demonstrated experience owning major security compliance and assurance programs such as FedRAMP, SOC 2, PCI DSS, or comparable regulatory frameworks, including direct engagement with auditors, assessors, and external stakeholders.

  • Strong technical understanding of modern cloud infrastructure, SaaS application security, identity and access management, vulnerability management, and security architecture. Ability to independently evaluate technical findings, control designs, and remediation approaches.

  • Proven ability to build and improve security programs, independently identify control gaps and emerging requirements, establish priorities, and translate security risks into actionable organizational plans.

  • Experience managing and developing security professionals, establishing high standards for quality and accountability, and leading programs across distributed teams.

  • Experience with third-party risk assessments, customer security diligence, and security risk management, including the ability to evaluate complex technical and contractual security requirements.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to influence engineering teams, business leaders, auditors, and external stakeholders without relying solely on formal authority.

Compensation:

$200,000/year - $260,000/year + equity + benefits

Note: This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels, and the actual base salary within that range will be determined by several components including but not limited to the individual's experience, skills, and qualifications.

Perks:

  • Employer paid group health insurance for you and your dependents

  • 401(k) plan with employer match (or equivalent for non US-based roles)

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Regular company-wide in-person events

  • Home office stipend, and more!

  • Follow Through

  • Deep Understanding

  • Whatever It Takes

  • Do Something Smart
